note: NOT here: dropping the three `k->chan_b = 0; k->chan_a = 0; k->buffers = 0;` stores.  They exist in the object (0xae729) and are what makes a partially built kernel safe to hand to the cleanup, but every one of them is overwritten by the allocation that follows on the only path the harness allocator can produce -- it never fails -- so the mutant is dead code removal and would read NOT CAUGHT while modelling nothing.

NOT here: swapping the ORDER of the two channel allocations, or of the two tap allocations.  Both pairs are the same size as each other, so the allocator's books are identical either way and no fixture can see the difference.  The object allocates chan_b before chan_a and chan_b's taps before chan_a's, which is read from 0xae7ba/0xae76e and 0xae743/0xae78f and is recorded here rather than tested.
